name: Critical minerals
summary: China extended its pause on some rare-earth export controls to 10 Jan 2027 on 9 Nov; April 2025 licensing stays in force
state: On 9 Nov China's commerce ministry extended its suspension of export controls on five rare earths and related technology, due to lapse on 10 Nov, to 10 Jan 2027, alongside paused curbs on some battery materials (Benchmark Minerals; The Star). Licensing controls imposed in April 2025 on seven rare earths, including dysprosium and terbium, remain in force, so Watch holds. Searches on 15 Nov found no production stoppages outside China linked to bans.
for_you: Makers of electric vehicles, wind turbines, electronics and defence equipment that rely on Chinese rare-earth magnets remain exposed to licensing delays and the January deadline.
rubric_hit: Watch: China's April 2025 rare-earth licensing controls in force; no export-ban production stoppages outside China for Alert

sources.title: Benchmark Minerals — China extends pause on rare earth and battery export controls until 2027
The Star — China extends suspension of rare earth export controls until January

why: Rare earths, gallium, germanium and graphite are chokepoints for chips, EVs and defence — and China dominates processing.
drivers: Export controls, trade disputes, mine outages, stockpiling.

rubric.alert: Export bans in force that are causing reported production stoppages outside China.
rubric.watch: New export controls announced or licensing slowed.
rubric.normal: No new export restrictions in the past month.
